claims_to_fix.statement: CPXM1 is raised in UC with a pooled log2FC of [gene=CPXM1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.8968], significant in seven of eight cohorts, and the stromal (fibroblast) origin is kept per cell. It is also raised in non-inflamed mucosa of MSCCR (log2FC [gene=CPXM1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.0059]), so part of the change tracks the disease itself, not only local inflammation; heterogeneity between cohorts is high. Genetics tested: no causal effect; protein not quantified.

claims_to_fix.statement: PCDH17 is a local marker of inflamed mucosa: in MSCCR it rises in inflamed biopsies (log2FC [gene=PCDH17; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.4831]) but only slightly in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=PCDH17; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.2776]), and it is up in all eight cohorts, with the endothelial origin kept per cell and adjustment holding.

claims.claim: the endothelial origin kept per cell
claims.reason: Record gives stromal lineage, not endothelial.
Only about 10% retained after composition adjustment.

claims_to_fix.statement: LILRA1 rises in inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=LILRA1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.3307]) with a small change in non-inflamed ([gene=LILRA1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.3679]); one Leuven cohort is not significant. The signal is largely neutrophil/myeloid: per neutrophil the inflamed-vs-uninflamed change is small, so the bulk rise is mostly influx of cells, not a change inside the tissue. Weak as a target.

claims_to_fix.statement: CHI3L1 is among the largest and most reproducible increases (inflamed MSCCR log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=3.8187], up in all eight cohorts), and the protein also rises (log2 ratio [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]). As a target it is weakened by mixed mouse colitis evidence (one study pathogenic, one protective) and an amber safety light for vital-organ expression; a marker first.

claims_to_fix.statement: CFB is raised across cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CFB; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.24], seven of eight cohorts significant; only the adult colon cohort misses significance), of epithelial origin and retained after composition adjustment, with a modest non-inflamed rise ([gene=CFB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.4765]) and a protein rise ([gene=CFB; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.238]). Against it: the safety light is red (very high expression in vital organs and a deficiency disease from gene loss), so systemic inhibition is a concern.

claims_to_fix.statement: RORC is modestly lower in UC, replicated in most cohorts (inflamed MSCCR log2FC [gene=RORC; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.4177]), but the paired inflamed-vs-non-inflamed change is nil ([gene=RORC; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-0.0627], not significant), so the loss reflects disease rather than local inflammation. The small size makes it a weak expression-supported target; restoring a Th17/ILC3 factor could be pro-inflammatory (interpretation, not tested here).

claims.reason: No cohort count for RORC cited.

claims_to_fix.statement: TUFM does not support the genetic hypothesis that inhibition helps: in inflamed MSCCR biopsies it is slightly lower, not higher (log2FC [gene=TUFM; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.188]), with no change in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=TUFM; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.0115]) and lower in several cohorts. The genetic record points to blood neutrophils and the single-cell lineage is epithelial, so the biopsy data neither confirm the predicted direction nor the cell. Weak candidate on expression grounds.

CEBPB supports its genetic rationale in expression: it is up in all cohorts that measure it, in inflamed MSCCR mucosa (log2FC [gene=CEBPB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.7059]) and more strongly in UNIFI ([gene=CEBPB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE206285; layer=rna; cohort=GSE206285; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=2.046]; array and RNA-seq sizes are not comparable). The change is mainly myeloid, so it may partly reflect immune-cell infiltration; it is a transcription factor, a harder drug route.

claims.claim: it is up in all cohorts that measure it
claims.reason: No cohort count for CEBPB cited.
